Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT A. Francisco Gold Condominium II Bldg, EDSA corner Mapagmahal St., Diliman, Quezon City OFFICE OF THE UNDERSECRETARY FOR LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG Opinion No. 07, s. 2010 19 January 2010 DIRECTOR FELICIDAD M. BITE DILQ City meld Office City Hall, Makati City Dear Dir. Bite: This refers to your letter dated 08 January 2010, whereby you have fumished this Office copies of the letters of Atty. Pio Kenneth I. Dasal, Makati City OIC, Law Department and Atty. Andresito X. Pornier, counsel of Mr. Emesto Moya, et al. As a brief backgrounder, Punong Barangay Joshua John Santiago of Barangay San Lorenzo, Makati City, was adjudged administratively guilty by the Sangguniang Panlungsod of Makati City for three (3) separate offenses and was penalized with six (6) months suspension for each administrative offense. Mr. Santiago appealed the said Decision of the Sanggunian to the Office of the President, which in tum issued another Decision exonerating Mr. Santiago from the two offenses, but finding him guilty of simple misconduct and meted upon the latter a six-month suspension from office. The crux of the matter in both letters refers to whether or not Punong Barangay Joshua John Santiago's re-assumption into his office without an implementing order contained in the Resolution dated 18 November 2009 denying the Motion for Reconsideration of the Appellees, vis-ä-vis the Declslon of the Office of the President dated 20 August 2009 is proper. This matter had already been resolved through this Department's issuance of DILQ Opinion No. 59, s. 2009, dated 04 December 2009, which clearly and categorically recognized Mr. Santiago's incumbency as Punong Barangay of Barangay San Lorenzo, Makati City. We quote the salient disposition thereof, viz: "We note In the unnumbered Memorandum that Punong Barangay Santiago has completed his service of the six (6) months suspension on 15 October a009. Having completed his service of the penalty of suspension, it is now a matter of right for him to re-assume his office aithout a directive from this Department. This is the reason why in the penultimate part of our unnumbered Memorandum, we stated that there should no longer be any legal impediment for the

-2- peaceful re-assumption of Punong Barangay Joshua John Santiago of his office. By requiring another order for the officiat re- assumption of Punong Barangay Santiago, we will be unduly prolonging his penalty of suspension beyond six (6) months, which is clearly contrary to the Decision of the Office of the President. Considering that he has already completely served his penalty of suspension of six (6) months, fairplay would dictate that the re-assumption of Punong Barangay Santiago should now be recognized even without any directive on the matter unless the Office of the President will issue an order to the contrary. Before addressing the matter, please be informed that the adverse camp, Mr. Ernesto Moya, should have questioned this Department's opinion through the provisions of the Rules of Court if the latter truly believed that DILQ Opinion No. 59, s. 2009 "does not have any factual or legal bases", instead of making his own legal interpretations. Emphasis should be made that while legal opinions do not have the force and effect of the law, courts nonetheless give great weight and respect to such executive interpretations. Coming now to the issue as to whether or not an implementing order from the Office of the President is still necessary to execute its decision and subsequent resolution, we reiterate our negative reply. An implementing order is a procedural technicality which ought to yield to the substantial contents of the Decision it purportedly seeks to implement. May it be stressed that the Decision of the Office of the President affirmed the finding of guilt. upon Punong Barangay Santiago on one administrative charge but exonerated him on the two (2) other administrative charges which each penalized the latter with a six-months suspension. Section 59 (d) of Civil Service Commission Resolution No. 991936, otherwise known as the Uniform Rules on Administrative Cases in the Civil Service (URACCS) explicitly provides: "SEC. 59. Effect of Exoneration on Certain Penalties: d. In case the penalty imposed is suspension, he shalt immediately be reinstated to his former post without loss of acniodty Aghts with payment of back salaries. xxx" Thus, supposing Mr. Santiago was already serving the second 6-month suspension, his exoneration therefrom automatically entitles him to re- assume his post. Hence, Mr. Santiago's re-assumption without any further implementing order is all the more justified as he had completely served the nrst 6•monü1 suspension, and was completely exonerated from the other two. Parenthetically, assuming the Court of Appeals rules in favor of the petitioner and completely reverses the Decision of the Office of the

-3- President and affirrns the Sangguniang Panlungsod Decision, Mr. Santiago will nonetheless have to serve the two separate periods of suspension. Meantime, without any adverse decision from the Court of Appeals, Mr. Santiago's full service of the penalty imposed on him as decreed by the Office of the President should be given respect. Perforce, please be informed that DILQ Opinion No. 59, s. 2009, stands, unless reversed by a proper court. Consequently, since Atty. Dasal has still requested guidance on the matter, please inform said officiai that Mr. Joshua John Santiago is the lawful local chief executive of Barangay San Lorenzo, Makati City. Collaterally, kindly advise Mr. Moya to respect this Department's recognition of Mr. Santiago and to refrain from being instigated to continue his illegal assumption as the said barangay's chief executive, lest he be charged administratively, criminally and civilly. If after all things have been said and done, and still this Department's herein action is still unheeded, then proper charges should thus be commenced against them who refuse to give respect to duly constituted authorties. Along that line and as a final note, please be guided by the statement of the Supreme Court in one case, viz: "Finally, for those who refuse to understand, no explanation is possible, but for those tvho understand, no explanation is necessary. (Fortich vs. Corona, G.R. No. 131457, November 17, 1998). We hope we have enlightened you on the matte. Very truly yours, AUSTERE A.
